neutral_facts.value: The prosecution case was that a dead body was found burning on a conical storage of cow dung cakes known as 'Bitora'. A post-mortem was conducted, revealing the body to be that of a female. DNA testing matched the remains with the DNA profile of the victim's father and mother, confirming the identity of the deceased. The FIR was lodged after the body was discovered. Witnesses stated that the deceased and the accused were familiar with each other and had gone to a village together. PW-4 and PW-5 claimed to have seen the accused with the deceased and her two minor children on January 3, 2004, and that the accused was seen on a Scooty with a gunny bag on it. The prosecution argued that the accused was the suspect, but the court found the evidence insufficient to establish guilt. The accused was acquitted due to the lack of conclusive evidence linking her to the crime.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that the prosecution's evidence was weak and full of contradictions. The witnesses PW-4 and PW-5 were inimical to the appellant as they had filed a suit for claiming the estate of Baburam, and their statements lacked corroboration. The evidence of last seen was deemed insufficient to sustain a conviction.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the legal principle that circumstantial evidence must form a complete and unbroken chain of circumstances pointing to the guilt of the accused, and that the prosecution must prove all the circumstances connecting the accused to the crime.

quotes.text: The Court held that when a case rests upon circumstantial evidence such evidence must satisfy the following tests: (1) the circumstances from which an inference of guilt is sought to be drawn, must be cogently and firmly established; (2) those circumstances should be of a definite tendency unerringly pointing towards guilt of the accused; (3) the circumstances, taken cumulatively, should form a chain so complete that there is no escape from the conclusion that within all human probability the crime was committed by the accused and none else.
